content.rationale:
One file under `src/`, holding the crossing and the split of its answer, because the read is one commitment with one observable: what comes back from the substrate, as pairs (`kywmkqlm`); where the file sits is the layout rule's, and so is the crate root's declaration of it (`szmuyqrq`). It crosses only through the runner (`zruxtxrv`) — `Jj::run` over a binary and a root the caller supplies, one spawned process per call, no library linkage — and imports nothing else: no store, no node document, no envelope, no crate module of its own. That is what keeps the read on the substrate side of the seam, and what lets the check stand on this module and the runner alone.

The crossing is one `jj log --no-graph` over the revset `::`, every visible change with the root included, and a template that carries each change's diff summary: the full change id, a tab, then for every entry of `diff.files()` the entry's source path, a tab, its target path, a tab, and a newline to end the change. The summary is asked for structurally rather than as rendered text, so the pairing is the summary's own: each changed entry names a source and a target, an ordinary change names the same path on both sides and so arrives with one path, and a rename or a copy names two and both sides arrive as the paths that change touched — the side it left and the side it reached, as two paths rather than one string standing in for both — never a changed set recomputed from the tree. The newline separates records and the tabs separate fields, so the answer splits by line into one change and by field, taken in pairs after the id, into that change's paths; a path the same change names twice is one path, and a change that touched nothing arrives with no paths rather than being dropped. Nothing narrows the set or its paths: no ownership test, no path filter, and no per-change read on the healthy path, because a read that kept only what the documents claim would have already answered the question the pass exists to ask, and a path narrowed to the ones a node lists would be the answer rather than the evidence. One crossing for the whole set is also what keeps the cost where the layer put it: the spawn count does not grow with the number of changes (`rkoktpwt`).

The fallbacks are degraded forms, not the healthy path. When the set read cannot run, the read falls back to the whole-set form the layer permits: the ids in one crossing, then each change's summary in a crossing of its own, so a failed set read does not become a set of changes taken as clean. When that fails too, the failure carried is the set read's, because that is the crossing that was supposed to work. The per-change form exists so that a change is not silently dropped, not so that it can become the read's ordinary work. What a change or a path that no form could serve means is settled elsewhere: a change the check cannot attribute is not thereby clean (`xotxspwp`).

It refuses content — no path's bytes cross this boundary, so an answer drawn from it can be about attribution and cannot be about comparison — and it refuses to judge: the ownership rule, the confrontation of a change's paths with the set its node claims, and whether a disagreement is a failure belong to the pass, not here. It refuses to render either: nothing is formatted, no line is chosen, and no status is decided. It returns the pairs or two distinguishable carried failures, a binary that could not be spawned and a crossing that ran and failed with its output verbatim, so a caller sees why rather than a bare refusal and no caller ever panics through this module (`uzzxlpsl`). What it leaves to its dependants: which module of the crate consumes it and how the pass spells its calls; what the pass prints for a disagreement, in what order and with what exit status; and which of the returned changes a caller iterates. None of those changes what comes back — every change with the paths it touched, and no content.
